assessment: This is a valuable study describing how rhabdomyosarcoma fusion-oncogenes, VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2, function at the genomic, transcriptional, and proteomic levels in multiple systems. The experimental data is convincing, supporting a model in which these fusion-oncogenes leverage TEAD transcriptional signatures independent of YAP/TAZ. This work offers new mechanistic insights into oncogenic gene fusion events and reveals potential therapeutic strategies for the treatment of rhabdomyosarcomas.
